# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```plantuml
class Course {

    name : String
}

}

    id : String
}

    name : String
    courses : List<Course>
    sectors : List<Sector>

    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session for the course on a given date, ensuring only one session per course per day. Returns the updated list of all sessions for the course.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a session with the given date already exists in sessions list.
  2. If it exists, return the current list unchanged.
  3. If not, create a new Session with the given date (empty participants, no trainer), add it to sessions list.
  4. Return the updated sessions list.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the new session (format: yyyy-MM-dd).
Output: List<Session> – the up-to-date list of sessions for this course after the operation.
Pre-condition: date is not null.
Post-condition: If no session exists for that date, a new Session is added to the sessions list. The returned list contains all sessions.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a document to the course's list of documents.
Algorithm: 
  1. Check if the document is already in the documents list (by name).
  2. If not present, add the document to the list.
  3. Return true if added, false if duplicate.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc: Document – the document to be added, must have a non-null name.
Output: boolean – true if the document was added, false if it already exists.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: If the document was not already in the list, it is added; otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) a session on a given date, but only if no participants are registered for that session. Returns true if successful, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the session in sessions list with the given date.
  2. If not found, return false.
  3. If found, check if registeredParticipants list of that session is empty.
  4. If empty, remove the session from sessions list and return true.
  5. If not empty, return false.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate, Participant
Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the session to cancel.
Output: boolean – true if session was removed, false if not found or has participants.
Pre-condition: date is not null.
Post-condition: If the session exists and has no participants, it is removed from sessions list. Otherwise, sessions list is unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Removes a document from the course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if the document exists in the documents list (by reference or name).
  2. If present, remove it and return true.
  3. If not present, return false.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc: Document – the document to be removed.
Output: boolean – true if the document was removed, false if not found.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: If the document was in the list, it is removed; otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session for the course on a given date, ensuring only one session per course per day. Returns the updated list of all sessions for the course.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a session with the given date already exists in sessions list.
  2. If it exists, return the current list unchanged.
  3. If not, create a new Session with the given date (empty participants, no trainer), add it to sessions list.
  4. Return the updated sessions list.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the new session (format: yyyy-MM-dd).
Output: List<Session> – the up-to-date list of sessions for this course after the operation.
Pre-condition: date is not null.
Post-condition: If no session exists for that date, a new Session is added to the sessions list. The returned list contains all sessions.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a document to the course's list of documents.
Algorithm: 
  1. Check if the document is already in the documents list (by name).
  2. If not present, add the document to the list.
  3. Return true if added, false if duplicate.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc: Document – the document to be added, must have a non-null name.
Output: boolean – true if the document was added, false if it already exists.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: If the document was not already in the list, it is added; otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels (removes) a session on a given date, but only if no participants are registered for that session. Returns true if successful, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the session in sessions list with the given date.
  2. If not found, return false.
  3. If found, check if registeredParticipants list of that session is empty.
  4. If empty, remove the session from sessions list and return true.
  5. If not empty, return false.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate, Participant
Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the session to cancel.
Output: boolean – true if session was removed, false if not found or has participants.
Pre-condition: date is not null.
Post-condition: If the session exists and has no participants, it is removed from sessions list. Otherwise, sessions list is unchanged.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Removes a document from the course's document list.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if the document exists in the documents list (by reference or name).
  2. If present, remove it and return true.
  3. If not present, return false.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc: Document – the document to be removed.
Output: boolean – true if the document was removed, false if not found.
Pre-condition: doc is not null.
Post-condition: If the document was in the list, it is removed; otherwise, the list remains unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the current trainer of this session with a new trainer, but only if the current date is strictly before the session date. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if today is strictly before session.date (today < session.date).
  2. If not, return false.
  3. If yes, set trainer = newTrainer and return true.
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer: Trainer – the new trainer to assign; today: LocalDate – the current date.
Output: boolean – true if trainer was replaced, false if today is not strictly before session date.
Pre-condition: newTrainer and today are not null.
Post-condition: If today < session.date, trainer is set to newTrainer; otherwise, trainer remains unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Registers a participant for this session, ensuring no duplicate enrollment. Returns true on success, false if already registered.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if the participant is already in registeredParticipants list (by ID).
  2. If found, return false.
  3. If not, add the participant to the list and return true.
Related Features: registeredParticipants (List<Participant>)
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p: Participant – the participant to register; today: LocalDate – the current date (not used in this operation per requirement, but provided for consistency).
Output: boolean – true if participant was added, false if already registered.
Pre-condition: p is not null.
Post-condition: If participant was not already in the list, they are added to registeredParticipants. Otherwise, the list is unchanged.

Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session, but only if the current date is strictly before the session date. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if today is strictly before session.date (today < session.date).
  2. If not, return false.
  3. If yes, set trainer = t and return true.
Related Features: date, trainer
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t: Trainer – the trainer to assign; today: LocalDate – the current date.
Output: boolean – true if trainer was assigned, false if today is not strictly before session date.
Pre-condition: t and today are not null.
Post-condition: If today < session.date, trainer is set to t; otherwise, trainer remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with a given ID and adds it to the school's sector list. Returns the newly created Sector object.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a sector with the given id already exists in sectors list.
  2. If it exists, return the existing sector (or null? Requirement implies creation, so we assume unique IDs – return existing for robustness).
  3. If not, create a new Sector with the given id, add it to sectors list, and return it.
Related Features: sectors (List<Sector>)
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id: String – the unique identifier for the new sector.
Output: Sector – the newly created sector or the existing one with the same ID.
Pre-condition: id is not null and not empty.
Post-condition: If no sector with the same id exists, a new Sector is added to sectors list and returned. Otherwise, the existing sector is returned.

School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a sector. If the course already belongs to a different sector, it is first removed from that sector. Returns true on success, false if course or sector not found.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the course by courseId in courses list; if not found, return false.
  2. Find the sector by sectorId in sectors list; if not found, return false.
  3. If course already belongs to a sector (course.sector != null), call sector.removeCourse(course) on the old sector.
  4. Call sector.addCourse(course) on the new sector.
  5. Set course.sector to the new sector.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses, sectors, Course.sector, Sector.courses, Sector::addCourse, Sector::removeCourse
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId: String – the ID of the course to assign; sectorId: String – the ID of the target sector.
Output: boolean – true if assignment succeeded, false if course or sector not found.
Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId are not null.
Post-condition: The course is removed from its previous sector (if any) and added to the specified sector. The course.sector is updated.

School::addCourse
Summary: Adds a new course to the school with a unique case-sensitive ID. Returns true on success, false if the ID already exists.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if any course in courses list has the same id (case-sensitive).
  2. If found, return false.
  3. If not found, create a new Course with the given id, add it to courses list, and return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>)
Related Classes: Course
Input: id: String – the unique case-sensitive identifier for the new course.
Output: boolean – true if course was added, false if ID already exists.
Pre-condition: id is not null and not empty.
Post-condition: If no course with the same id exists, a new Course is added to courses list. Otherwise, courses list is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

   * Summary: Adds a new session for the course on a given date, ensuring only one session per course per day. Returns the updated list of all sessions for the course.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Check if a session with the given date already exists in sessions list.
   *   2. If it exists, return the current list unchanged.
   *   3. If not, create a new Session with the given date (empty participants, no trainer), add it to sessions list.
   *   4. Return the updated sessions list.
   * Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
   * Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
   * Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the new session (format: yyyy-MM-dd).
   * Output: List<Session> – the up-to-date list of sessions for this course after the operation.
   * Pre-condition: date is not null.
   * Post-condition: If no session exists for that date, a new Session is added to the sessions list. The returned list contains all sessions.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model dateDataType="edu.trainingSchool.LocalDate" dateRequired="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Session> addSession(final LocalDate date)
  {
    // Check if a session with the given date already exists
    for (Session session : getSessions()) {
      if (date.equals(session.getDate())) {
        return getSessions();
      }
    }
    // Create a new Session with the given date
    Session newSession = TrainingSchoolFactory.eINSTANCE.createSession();
    newSession.setDate(date);
    // Add it to the sessions list
    getSessions().add(newSession);
    // Return the updated sessions list
    return getSessions();
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Cancels (removes) a session on a given date, but only if no participants are registered for that session. Returns true if successful, false otherwise.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Find the session in sessions list with the given date.
   *   2. If not found, return false.
   *   3. If found, check if registeredParticipants list of that session is empty.
   *   4. If empty, remove the session from sessions list and return true.
   *   5. If not empty, return false.
   * Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
   * Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
   * Input: date: LocalDate – the date of the session to cancel.
   * Output: boolean – true if session was removed, false if not found or has participants.
   * Pre-condition: date is not null.
   * Post-condition: If the session exists and has no participants, it is removed from sessions list. Otherwise, sessions list is unchanged.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model dateDataType="edu.trainingSchool.LocalDate" dateRequired="true"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean cancelSession(final LocalDate date)
  {
    // Find the session with the given date
    for (Session session : getSessions()) {
      if (date.equals(session.getDate())) {
        // Check if registeredParticipants list is empty
        if (session.getRegisteredParticipants().isEmpty()) {
          // Remove the session from sessions list
          getSessions().remove(session);
          return true;
        } else {
          return false;
        }
      }
    }
    // Session not found
    return false;
  }

  {
    // Check if the document is already in the documents list (by name)

        return false;
      }
    }
    // Add the document to the list
    getDocuments().add(doc);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->

public boolean assignTrainer(final Trainer t, final LocalDate today) {
    // 1. Check if today is strictly before session.date
    if (today.isBefore(this.date)) {
        // 3. If yes, set trainer = t and return true
        setTrainer(t);
        return true;
    }
    // 2. If not, return false
    return false;

public boolean replaceTrainer(final Trainer newTrainer, final LocalDate today) {
    // 1. Check if today is strictly before session.date
    if (today.isBefore(this.date)) {
        // 3. If yes, set trainer = newTrainer and return true
        setTrainer(newTrainer);
        return true;
    }
    // 2. If not, return false
    return false;
}

public boolean registerParticipant(final Participant p, final LocalDate today) {
    // 1. Check if the participant is already in registeredParticipants list (by ID)
    for (Participant registered : getRegisteredParticipants()) {
        if (registered.getId().equals(p.getId())) {
            // 2. If found, return false
            return false;
        }
    }
    // 3. If not, add the participant to the list and return true
    getRegisteredParticipants().add(p);
    return true;
}

You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in <Operations> with a specfication.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pesudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.
```

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Operation Specifications
School::assignCourseToSector
Summary: Assigns a course to a sector. If the course already belongs to a sector, it is first removed from that sector. Returns true on success, false if either course or sector not found.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the course by courseId in courses list. If not found, return false.
  2. Find the sector by sectorId in sectors list. If not found, return false.
  3. If the course already has a sector (course.sector != null):
     a. Call course.sector.removeCourse(course).
  4. Call sector.addCourse(course).
  5. Set course.sector = sector.
  6. Return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>), sectors (List<Sector>), Course::sector, Sector::addCourse, Sector::removeCourse
Related Classes: Course, Sector
Input: courseId : String - the ID of the course to assign; sectorId : String - the ID of the target sector.
Output: boolean - true if assignment was successful, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: courseId and sectorId correspond to existing Course and Sector in the school.
Post-condition: If successful, the course is removed from its previous sector (if any) and added to the new sector. The course's sector attribute points to the new sector.

School::addCourse
Summary: Adds a new course to the school with the given case-sensitive unique ID. Returns true on success, false if a course with the same ID already exists.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a course with the given id already exists in courses list.
  2. If yes, return false.
  3. Otherwise, create a new Course with the given id, empty documents list, null sector, and empty sessions list.
  4. Add the new course to courses list.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: courses (List<Course>)
Related Classes: Course
Input: id : String - the case-sensitive unique identifier for the course. Must not be null or empty.
Output: boolean - true if course was added, false if a course with the same ID already exists.
Pre-condition: id != null and id != "".
Post-condition: If successful, courses list contains the new Course. Otherwise, courses list remains unchanged.

School::addSector
Summary: Creates a new sector with the given unique ID and adds it to the school's list of sectors. Returns the newly created Sector.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a sector with the given id already exists in sectors list. If yes, return null (or throw exception, but per requirement assume return null for failure).
  2. Otherwise, create a new Sector with the given id and empty courses list.
  3. Add the new sector to sectors list.
  4. Return the new sector.
Related Features: sectors (List<Sector>)
Related Classes: Sector
Input: id : String - the unique identifier for the sector. Must not be null or empty.
Output: Sector - the newly created Sector object, or null if a sector with the same ID already exists.
Pre-condition: id != null and id != "".
Post-condition: If successful, sectors list contains the new Sector. Otherwise, sectors list remains unchanged.

  3. Return true.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title trainingSchool Model

class Course {
    id : String
    documents : List<Document>
    sector : Sector
    sessions : List<Session>
    addDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
    addSession(date : LocalDate) : List<Session>
    cancelSession(date : LocalDate) : boolean
    removeDocument(doc : Document) : boolean
}
class Document {
    name : String
}
class Participant {
}
abstract class Person {
    id : String
}
class School {
    name : String
    courses : List<Course>
    sectors : List<Sector>
    addCourse(id : String) : boolean
    addSector(id : String) : Sector
    assignCourseToSector(courseId : String, sectorId : String) : boolean
}
class Sector {
    id : String
    courses : List<Course>
    addCourse(course : Course) : void
    removeCourse(course : Course) : void
}
class Session {
    date : LocalDate
    registeredParticipants : List<Participant>
    trainer : Trainer
    assignTrainer(t : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    registerParticipant(p : Participant, today : LocalDate) : boolean
    replaceTrainer(newTrainer : Trainer, today : LocalDate) : boolean
}
class Trainer {
    contractor : boolean
}

Course --> "*" Document : documents
Course --> Sector : sector  'opposite: courses
Course *-- "*" Session : sessions
Participant --|> Person
School *-- "*" Course : courses
School *-- "*" Sector : sectors
Sector --> "*" Course : courses  'opposite: sector
Session --> "*" Participant : registeredParticipants
Session --> Trainer : trainer
Trainer --|> Person
@enduml
```

# Operation Specifications
Session::assignTrainer
Summary: Assigns a trainer to this session, but only if the current date is strictly before the session's date. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If today is not strictly before this.date (i.e., today >= this.date), return false.
  2. If this.trainer is already set, return false (use replaceTrainer for replacement).
  3. Otherwise, set this.trainer = t and return true.
Related Features: date (LocalDate), trainer (Trainer)
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: t : Trainer - the trainer to assign; today : LocalDate - the current date.
Output: boolean - true if trainer was assigned, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: t != null, today != null.
Post-condition: If successful, this.trainer is set to t. Otherwise, this.trainer remains unchanged.

Session::registerParticipant
Summary: Registers a participant for this session. Ensures no duplicate enrollment for the same participant. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if p is already in registeredParticipants list. If yes, return false.
  2. Add p to registeredParticipants list.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: registeredParticipants (List<Participant>)
Related Classes: Participant
Input: p : Participant - the participant to register; today : LocalDate - the current date (included for consistency but not used in this operation).
Output: boolean - true if participant was registered, false if already registered.
Pre-condition: p != null.
Post-condition: If successful, p is added to registeredParticipants list. Otherwise, list remains unchanged.

Session::replaceTrainer
Summary: Replaces the trainer for this session, but only if the current date is strictly before the session's date. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. If today is not strictly before this.date (i.e., today >= this.date), return false.
  2. If this.trainer is null, return false (use assignTrainer for initial assignment).
  3. Otherwise, set this.trainer = newTrainer and return true.
Related Features: date (LocalDate), trainer (Trainer)
Related Classes: Trainer, LocalDate
Input: newTrainer : Trainer - the new trainer to assign; today : LocalDate - the current date.
Output: boolean - true if trainer was replaced, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: newTrainer != null, today != null.
Post-condition: If successful, this.trainer is set to newTrainer. Otherwise, this.trainer remains unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Course::addSession
Summary: Adds a new session for the course on a given date. Only one session per course per day allowed. Returns the updated list of all sessions for the course.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if a session with the given date already exists in sessions list.
  2. If yes, return the current sessions list unchanged.
  3. Otherwise, create a new Session with the given date, empty registeredParticipants list, and no trainer.
  4. Add the new session to sessions list.
  5. Return the sessions list.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the session to add (format: yyyy-MM-dd). Must not be null.
Output: List<Session> - the course's up-to-date list of sessions.
Pre-condition: date != null.
Post-condition: If no session with the same date existed, a new Session is added to sessions. The returned list reflects the current state.

Course::removeDocument
Summary: Removes a document from the course's list of referenced documents.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if doc is null or if doc does not exist in the documents list.
  2. If yes, return false.
  3. Otherwise, remove doc from documents list and return true.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to be removed, must exist in the course's document list.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully removed, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc != null and doc exists in documents list.
Post-condition: If successful, documents list no longer contains the document and its size decreases by 1.

Course::cancelSession
Summary: Cancels a session on a given date, but only if the session has no registered participants. Returns true if cancellation was successful, false otherwise.
Algorithm:
  1. Find the session in sessions list with the given date.
  2. If not found, return false.
  3. If the session has any registered participants (registeredParticipants is not empty), return false.
  4. Otherwise, remove the session from sessions list and return true.
Related Features: sessions (List<Session>)
Related Classes: Session, LocalDate
Input: date : LocalDate - the date of the session to cancel (format: yyyy-MM-dd).
Output: boolean - true if session was cancelled, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: date != null.
Post-condition: If successful, the session with the given date is removed from sessions list. Otherwise, sessions list remains unchanged.

Course::addDocument
Summary: Adds a document to the course's list of referenced documents.
Algorithm:
  1. Check if doc is null or if doc already exists in the documents list.
  2. If yes, return false.
  3. Otherwise, add doc to documents list and return true.
Related Features: documents (List<Document>)
Related Classes: Document
Input: doc : Document - the document to be added, must not be null and must not already exist in the course's document list.
Output: boolean - true if the document was successfully added, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: doc != null and doc not already in documents list.
Post-condition: If successful, documents list contains the new document and its size increases by 1.

# Requirement
```text
Either in a school that performs the following functions: Develop catalogs that describe the courses and give the estimated dates of the sessions (date format : "2025-02-06"). Each course has an unique id. Register people have their unique id and can participate in the sessions. Determine the trainers who will lead the sessions. Each trainer has an unique id. Some sessions may be led by individual contractors. Some courses are assigned and organized into sectors which have unique ids. The courses use referenced documents with names. The system can upload/delete documents to/from courses. The school has a unique name.
Functional requirement:
1. Add a course. The school can add a new course by providing a case-sensitive unique ID. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, false.

2. Assign a course to a sector. A course can belong to exactly one sector at a time. When assigning a course to a new sector, the system must first remove it from its current sector (if any) before adding it to the new one. Return true if successful; otherwise, false.

3. Manage the session schedule of a cours. For any course, the system can add or cancel sessions by providing a specific date (format: yyyy-MM-dd). When adding, ensure only one session per course per day.  The operation returns the course's up-to-date list of sessions. When canceling, only sessions without participants may be removed. The operation returns true on success; otherwise, it returns false.

4. Assign or replace a trainer for a session. The trainer assignment or replacement must be done strictly before the session's start date (i.e., the current date must be strictly earlier than the session date; same-day operations are not allowed). The operation returns a boolean value indicating success.

5. Register a participant for a session. A participant may enroll in any session by providing a date and course ID. The call adds the participant to the specified session, ensuring no duplicate enrollments for the same participant. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
```

```java
            return getSessions();
```

```java
public boolean cancelSession(final LocalDate date)
```
